first_answers.luna:
A 2 MeV gamma ray carries momentum \(p=E/c\). The recoil energy is \(E_r=p^2/(2M)=E^2/(2Mc^2)\). For an atom of mass 10 amu, \(Mc^2\approx 10\times 931.5\) MeV, so \(E_r\approx 4/(2\times 9315)\) MeV \(\approx 215\) eV.

ANSWER: D
first_answers.nemo:
The recoil energy of an atom after gamma-ray emission is given by \( E_{\text{recoil}} = \frac{E_\gamma^2}{2 m c^2} \).  
For a gamma-ray energy \( E_\gamma = 2 \text{ MeV} \) and an atom of mass number 10 (mass \( m = 10 \, u = 10 \times 931.5 \text{ MeV}/c^2 = 9315 \text{ MeV}/c^2 \)):  
\[
E_{\text{recoil}} = \frac{(2 \text{ MeV})^2}{2 \times 9315 \text{ MeV}} = \frac{4}{18630} \text{ MeV} \approx 2.147 \times 10^{-4} \text{ MeV} = 214.7 \text{ eV}.
\]  
This matches option D.

ANSWER: D
